### [A Statement on Art and Resistance](https://dodge.zimmerli.rutgers.edu/)

The [Norton and Nancy Dodge Collection of Nonconformist Art from the Soviet Union](https://dodge.zimmerli.rutgers.edu/) is a testimony to the strength of the human spirit under the oppressive rule of totalitarian regimes worldwide. The Collection presents artists from Ukraine, Belarus and Russia, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan, who stood for their freedom of expression, despite the harassment and prosecution that they faced from Soviet-era authorities. These artists’ resistance to the constraints imposed on all aspects of life at that time gains new relevance today and should strengthen our resolve to preserve the open societies they fought for. 

Leonhard Lapin, _Holes in the Head_, 1972. Gouache on paper. Norton and Nancy Dodge Collection of Nonconformist Art from the Soviet Union. Collection Zimmerli Art Museum at Rutgers University. Photo Peter Jacobs.

## Featured Holdings

### American Art

The Zimmerli's American art collection, numbering more than 16,500 objects, includes paintings, sculpture, works on paper (prints, drawings, and photographs), and decorative arts. 

[Learn More](https://zimmerli.rutgers.edu/collections/american-art)

### European Art

The Zimmerli’s collection of European art in all media ranges in date from the Renaissance to the present and totals close to 10,000 objects, with its primary strength in French nineteenth-century works on paper, notably prints and rare books. 

[Learn More](https://zimmerli.rutgers.edu/collections/european-art)

### Soviet Nonconformist Art and Arts of Eurasia

The Zimmerli’s Soviet Nonconformist art and arts of Eurasia holdings contain over 22,000 objects and provide a unique overview from the fourteenth century to the present.

[Learn More](http://live-zimmerli.pantheonsite.io/collections/russian-art-soviet-nonconformist-art)

### Asian Art

The Asian collection is comprised of prints, books, and photographs, primarily from nineteenth-century Japan. Highlights include over 200 woodcuts from the late eighteenth through the twentieth centuries.

[Learn More](https://zimmerli.rutgers.edu/collections/asian-art)

### Original Illustrations for Children's Literature

The Collection of Original Illustrations for Children’s Literature has nearly 4,000 works, including original drawings and preparatory materials that document the book making process.

[Learn More](https://zimmerli.rutgers.edu/collections/original-illustrations-childrens-literature)

## About The Zimmerli

The Zimmerli Art Museum is one of the largest and most distinguished university-based museums in the country. It collects, preserves, researches, and exhibits world-class works of art to provide the university community and diverse regional, national, international audiences with direct experience of the visual arts. Scholarly activities make art accessible through exhibitions, publications, and educational programs.

# Creativity 
Lives Here

There's art for everyone at Mobile Museum of Art.

[Visit Us](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/visit/ 'Visit Us') 

[scroll down](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/# 'favicon icon')

### At Mobile Museum of Art, our mission is simple:

## To Bring People Together and 
Inspire Creativity Through the Power of Art

## GATEWAY: From Graffiti to Gallery

Featuring 28 significant works, _GATEWAY_ traces the journey from street art pioneers Basquiat, Haring, and Scharf and sets the stage for two of today’s leading voices, Banksy and KAWS.

Open through Sept. 1, 2027

[Special Exhibition](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/exhibitions/gateway/ 'Special Exhibition') 

## Aminah Robinson: Journeys Home

Drawing upon Robinson’s historical research, folklore, and personal narrative, the exhibition presents a visual memoir of the artist’s life and a compelling tableau of the African American experience.

Open through Jan. 9, 2027

[Special Exhibition](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/exhibitions/aminah-robinson-journeys-home-a-visual-memoir/ 'Special Exhibition ') 

## Timeless Hats by Susie Mae Pugh-Williams

This exhibition contains over two dozen hats that were made by Mrs. Williams or that she admired and drew inspiration from for her own creations.

Open through Jan. 30, 2027

[Special Exhibition](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/exhibitions/timeless-hats/ 'Special Exhibition') 

## Handle with Care

_Handle with Care_ is a new interactive exhibition exploring all the potential of what we take for granted. In this exhibition, artists Calder Kamin (Austin, TX) and Jacob Reptile (New Orleans, LA) transform trash into soft and complex sculptures to create a new kind of environment.

Open through Mar. 27, 2027

[Special Exhibition](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/exhibitions/handle-with-care/ 'Special Exhibition ') 

Classes & Education

## Discover, Learn, Create

At The Museum School, learning never stops. From engaging school tours to hands-on art classes and workshops, we offer educational programs for learners of all ages. Whether you're a student exploring creativity for the first time or an adult rediscovering the joy of making, our programs are designed to inspire, educate, and enrich.

[See Classes](https://www.mobilemuseumofart.com/learn/adults/ 'See Classes')

Our Permanent Collection

## Timeless Creations in Every Medium

Mobile Museum of Art’s permanent collection consists of an assemblage of American, European, African, and Asian art, including paintings, sculptures, prints, drawings, and decorative art. Highlights include: 19th-century American landscapes, realist paintings from the WPA era, contemporary international studio glass, turned wood, and ceramics.

## Winter Art Camp: Storytelling Through Art!

Dates: December 21, 22, 23, 28, 29, 30, 31, 2026, and January 4, 2027 All works of art have a story to tell! Spend the winter break exploring the many ways artists tell stories about people, places, animals, and the world around us. Explore the playful picture book illustrations of Sophie Blackall, the passionate conservation photographs of Carlton Ward Jr., and the wonderfully weird treasures of Florida’s past from the exhibition, Floridiana: Material Culture from the Sunshine State. Be inspired to tell your own stories by drawing, painting, collaging, and more!

[LEARN MORE](https://omart.org/learn/winter_art_camp/)

## The Wild Path: Connecting the Florida We Don’t See Photographs by Carlton Ward Jr.

The Wild Path: Connecting the Florida We Don’t See presents 70 works by National Geographic conservation photographer Carlton Ward Jr., focused on wild Florida.

[Visit Today](https://orlando.tamretail.net/Events.aspx?display=ga)

## On View Now: Hello, Sophie!: The Artwork of SophieBlackall

Sophie Blackall is a Brooklyn-based Australian artist. She has illustrated over fifty books for children, including the New York Times best-selling Ivy and Bean series, and has twice received the Randolph Caldecott Medal, in 2016 for Finding Winnie and in 2019 for Hello Lighthouse.

[Visit Today!](https://orlando.tamretail.net/Events.aspx?display=ga)

## On view now Floridiana: Material Culture from the Sunshine State

Florida has long been a place of escape, and the souvenirs visitors took home during its mid-century heyday—hotel ashtrays, rubber alligators, roadside attraction brochures—embodied memories of carefree days in the Sunshine State.

[Visit Today!](https://orlando.tamretail.net/Events.aspx?display=ga)

Join us for a fun night of art!

[Learn more](https://mofa.fsu.edu/on-view/#brxe-mljttu)

### Friendly Arbitration: Honoré Daumier on Crime, Justice, and Punishment

Opening on July 23, _Friendly Arbitration_ examines Honoré Daumier’s (1808–1879) subversive use of lithography and wood engraving as tools for artistic innovation and social critique in nineteenth-century France. Bringing together original prints from his popular series on lawyers, the legal system, and crime and punishment, the exhibition explores how his satirical caricatures challenged judicial authority, exposed social inequities, and helped reshape the fields of art and journalism.

## Make the most of your visit to the Hunter

Perched on an 80-foot bluff overlooking the Tennessee River, the Hunter Museum of American Art features a collection of nearly 3,000 works illustrating the diversity of the American story and the creativity of the American spirit. Galleries filled with paintings and drawings, sculptures and new media will bring out your inner artist. Visit with your family and friends to discover what makes the Hunter Museum an experience unlike any other!

Parking is available at the Hunter Museum parking lot, 500 feet from the entrance to the museum. The parking lot is wheelchair accessible. Museum guests can park for **three hours for free** by registering their vehicle using their license plate number.

Accessibility

The Hunter is universally accessible. Wheelchairs and strollers are available free of charge at Visitor Services, and service dogs are welcome in the building. We also offer sensory-friendly maps to assist youth on the Autism Spectrum or with sensory processing disorders.

### Art connects us to each other and the world we live in

We believe that art allows us a window into the perspectives, experiences, and viewpoints of others.  As we strive to better engage our diverse audiences in active dialogues about the meaning and relevance of American art, the Hunter continues to reimagine and reinterpret American art itself.

Our programs and exhibitions are shaped by our commitment to representing a variety of experiences, cultures, and perspectives in hopes that visitors see art with new eyes—as a way to better understand both where we’ve been and where we are today.

[About The Hunter](https://www.huntermuseum.org/about)

## See the world without leaving Bloomington

Take a trip around the world—and through time—when you walk through the doors of our iconic building in the heart of the IU Bloomington campus. Come discover treasures from antiquity and sub-Saharan Africa; paintings by Monet, Picasso, and Pollock; works from contemporary artists; and so much more.

As a modern teaching museum, we’re using art to change the way you’ll understand the human experience. Come see what we have to offer.

# Home

---

## ******Taste of Tall Grass******

Taste of Tall Grass is the first season of Tall Grass, our new restaurant opening on State Street. Rather than wait for the permanent space to be finished, Chef Elena Terry is starting upstairs in MMoCA’s rooftop lounge with dinner Thursday through Saturday, Saturday brunch, and special collaborative programs.

[Learn More about Taste of Tall Grass](https://www.mmoca.org/tallgrass/)

## ******MMoCA Cinema • _Our Land_******

The first documentary feature from acclaimed Argentinean filmmaker Lucrecia Martel (Zama, The Headless Woman) examines the murder of Indigenous activist Javier Chocobar, and the centuries-old legacy of land and property theft across Latin America.

[Learn More about MMoCA Cinema • Our Land](https://www.mmoca.org/events/mmoca-cinema-our-land-2/)

## **Drink and Draw**

Enjoy a creative evening of drawing and drinks at the Museum. Jane Fasse, Senior Adjunct Instructor at Edgewood College, leads a figure drawing session in the Rooftop Lounge, where you can learn to draw the human form with body-inclusive nude models in various poses. Admission includes one drink, and a cash bar is available for additional refreshments.

[Learn More about Drink and Draw](https://www.mmoca.org/events/drink-and-draw-8/)

## Accidentally Wes Anderson

Call for Submissions 
Sep 28 – Nov 15, 2026 
Photos and Videos

In partnership with Accidentally Wes Anderson (AWA), see Racine through a more curious lens. Submit photographs of colorful, quirky, and wonderfully unexpected places—from roadside attractions and supper clubs to lighthouses, landmarks, and everything in between. Selected submissions will be featured in a [2027 exhibition](https://www.ramart.org/event/accidentally-wes-anderson-adventures-in-wisconsin/) at RAM Downtown that explores Wisconsin through filmmaker Wes Anderson’s distinctive visual style, alongside works from the museum’s collection.

[Learn More](https://www.ramart.org/event/accidentally-wes-anderson-adventures-in-wisconsin/)

# Museum of Wisconsin Art

## A Different Kind of Museum

## Art Museum in Wisconsin

# American art through the lens of a single state

At the Museum of Wisconsin Art, we believe that where we live is important and we are passionate about everything Wisconsin.

We also believe enjoying art should be easy and welcoming, not an exclusive privilege. That’s why instead of single-day admission, your entrance fee is an affordable membership providing unlimited museum access for an entire year. [Learn more](https://wisconsinart.org/mowa-memberships/)

## Exhibitions On View

### Lewis Hine

Pictures America

Opening Party

October 24 | 2:00–4:00

The photographs of Lewis Hine—the “father of documentary photography”—expose the harsh realities faced by immigrants, children, and the working class in the early decades of the twentieth century.

[View Details](https://wisconsinart.org/exhibitions/lewis-hine/)

[View All Exhibitions](https://wisconsinart.org/exhibitions)

## Exhibitions On View

### Edward Steichen

In Exaltation of Flowers

Opening Party

October 24 | 2:00–4:00

While Edward Steichen was best known for his photography, he was also an accomplished painter early in his career.

[View Details](https://wisconsinart.org/exhibitions/lewis-hines/)

[View All Exhibitions](https://wisconsinart.org/exhibitions)

### Locations

**A network of locations and community partners**

MOWA can be found around the state with two permanent venues—the West Bend “Mothership” and MOWA | DTN in downtown Milwaukee—and two partnering community organizations that make its programs and collections accessible and free.

[MOWA | West Bend\\ \\ _The Mothership_](https://wisconsinart.org/mowa-locations/#location 'Learn More')

[MOWA | DTN\\ \\ _Milwaukee_](https://wisconsinart.org/mowa-locations/#location 'Learn More')

[MOWA on the Lake\\ \\ _Milwaukee_](https://wisconsinart.org/mowa-locations/#lake 'Learn More') [MOWA | Governor’s Residence\\ \\ Madison](https://wisconsinart.org/mowa-locations/#governorsresidence 'Learn More')

ART BRIDGES

MOWA has an ongoing partnership with Art Bridges, a foundation established by Alice Walton in conjunction with the Art Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville, AR. In an effort to expand access to American art, Art Bridges provides loans from its growing permanent collection to participating institutions, along with financial support for initiatives that connect local audiences and communities.

Land Acknowledgment Statement

The Museum of Wisconsin Art stands on the ancestral lands of the Ho-Chunk, Menominee, and Potawatomi people. We pay respects to their elders past and present and acknowledge the Ho-Chunk, Menominee, and Potawatomi people who have stewarded this land through the generations.

## Celebrate the Arts and Culture of Wisconsin

**To our members, donors, and community partners—thank you for being an important part of our journey.**

Your contribution to the MOWA Fund will help MOWA continue to fulfill its special role in the arts and culture of our state for generations to come.

[Support MOWA](https://wisconsinart.org/wisconsin-art-fund/ 'Support MOWA')

jsonLd.description: <h4>Art+Wellness | What the Body Can Hold: The Form and Flow of Gesture<br /> Maria Soledad Gillespie</h4> <p class="p1">Inspired by Edward Steichen’s work In Exaltation of Flowers, choreographer Maria Soledad Gillespie explores the connections between dance and visual art as records of the human experience and as living, expressive forms. Through movement, she responds to Steichen’s work and considers how an image can be translated into the language of the body.</p> <p> </p>
jsonLd.name: Art+Wellness | What the Body Can Hold: The Form and Flow of Gesture

jsonLd.description: <h3><b>Champagne Shopping<br /> </b>December 4–6</h3> <p class="p1">Explore a curated selection of museum-branded items, works of fine art, and artist-driven goods.<sup>*</sup> Find covet-worthy gifts for everyone on your list or treat yourself to something special.</p> <p class="p1">All members are included!</p> <p class="p2"><span class="s1">one<br /> </span><b>5% off</b></p> <p class="p2"><span class="s1">two<br /> </span><b>10% off</b></p> <p class="p2"><span class="s1">Crew<br /> </span><b>20% off</b></p> <p class="p3">Member+ and above <span class="s2"><b>30% off</b></span></p> <p> </p> <h3><span class="s1"> </span></h3> <p> </p>
jsonLd.name: Champagne Shopping

jsonLd.description: <h4>Wisconsin Roots: The Documentary Photography of Lewis Hine</h4> <p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">Join David Travis, founding curator of the photography department at The Art Institute of Chicago, for a presentation about Oshkosh-born Lewis Hine and his pioneering work documenting child labor abuses, new arrivals at Ellis Island, and the essential quality of the American worker.</p> <figure id="attachment_7594" class="thumbnail wp-caption alignnone" style="width: 221px;"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="alignnone  wp-image-7594" src="https://wisconsinart.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Travis-1239-version2.jpg" alt="" width="221" height="201" srcset="https://wisconsinart.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Travis-1239-version2.jpg 800w, https://wisconsinart.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Travis-1239-version2-300x273.jpg 300w, https://wisconsinart.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Travis-1239-version2-768x698.jpg 768w, https://wisconsinart.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/David-Travis-1239-version2-600x545.jpg 600w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 221px) 100vw, 221px" /></figure> <p> </p> <p><strong>FREE for members</strong></p> <p> </p> <p> </p>
jsonLd.name: Wisconsin Roots: The Documentary Photography of Lewis Hine

jsonLd.description: <h4><b>Second Saturday | </b><b></b><span class="s1"><b>Made with Love</b></span></h4> <p class="p2"><span class="s3">Explore how artists honor their friends and family, then make a portrait, floral arrangement, or memory box to honor a special someone.</span></p> <p> </p> <h3><span class="s1"> </span></h3> <p> </p>
jsonLd.name: Second Saturday | Made with Love

jsonLd.description: <h4 data-pm-slice="1 1 []">The Art of Himmeli</h4> <p>Discover the Nordic tradition of himmeli with artist Rachael Gonzalez. Traditionally made from straw and associated with good fortune and prosperity, these geometric ornaments have also been described as “spirit traps,” believed to invite positive energy into the home. In this cozy, hands-on workshop, participants will learn the basics of constructing their own himmeli to take home—just in time for the holiday season. No previous experience is necessary.</p> <a class="maxbutton-1 maxbutton maxbutton-blue" target="_blank" rel="noopener" href="https://34727.blackbaudhosting.com/34727/Adult-Studio-Class-Himmeli"><span class='mb-text'>REGISTER TODAY!</span></a> <p> </p> <p>$40 with membership | All supplies included</p>
jsonLd.name: The Art of Himmeli

jsonLd.name: Mini Makers | Celebrate in Style

jsonLd.description: <h4>Art+Wellness | Through Ellis Island: The Immigration Experience<br /> Vicki Tobias</h4> <h6>Lewis Hine’s photographs of the Ellis Island experience provide insight into the history of U.S. immigration. Join historian and genealogist Vicki Tobias, as she examines why immigrants left their homelands, the experience at Ellis Island, and how documentation from the time traces a family’s origin.</h6> <p> </p>
jsonLd.name: Art+Wellness | Through Ellis Island: The Immigration Experience

# Haggerty Museum of Art

# **Where art and ideas come alive.**

The Haggerty Museum of Art welcomes all visitors to explore, learn, and engage with art—free of charge and open to all. Dive into our [exhibitions](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/exhibitions.php), [events](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/events.php), and [educational opportunities](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/educational-programs.php), or [learn more about us](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/about.php).

**Plan your visit** 
Ready to stop by? Find everything you need—hours, directions, parking, and accessibility—so your visit to the Haggerty is effortless and inspiring. [Start planning your visit](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/hours.php).

**What’s on view** 
Discover the exhibitions shaping conversations on campus and across Milwaukee. [Take a closer look at what’s currently on display](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/exhibitions.php).

**Attend an event** 
Experience the museum in new ways through conversations, gatherings, and special programs. [See what’s coming up and join us](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/events.php).

**Learn with us** 
Whether you’re a student, educator, or curious visitor, you’ll find engaging ways to connect with art. [Explore our learning programs and resources](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/educational-programs.php).

**Support the Haggerty** 
Help keep the museum free and open to all. [Explore the ways you can give](https://www.marquette.edu/haggerty-museum/support.php) and make an impact on exhibitions, learning programs, and community access.

# Your Free Art Museum for 30 Years! (1996-2026)

Welcome to the Marianna Kistler Beach Museum of Art. The museum celebrates regional art and brings art and artists from around the world to the heart of Kansas. Our collection continues to focus on the art of Kansas and the region.

### **Beach Museum of Art Fall 2026 classes - registration is open.**
